test_vectors.vectors: First sequences 0, 1, 43, u64::MAX - 1, u64::MAX; count limits 0, 1, 7, usize::MAX; byte limits 0, 1, usize::MAX.
test_vectors.assertions: Zero count is ConstraintViolation with canonical runtime metadata; valid options and empty-pop state remain unchanged. Default options are covered.

test_vectors.vectors: Sequences 40, 41, 42 with weights 0, 1, usize::MAX and zero buffered-byte capacity.
test_vectors.assertions: Every head is delivered directly and pending accounting stays zero.

test_vectors.vectors: Arrival order 12, 11, 10; count capacity 2; byte capacity 7; head weight usize::MAX.
test_vectors.assertions: A full queue rejects another future sequence but accepts its head; output order is 10, 11, 12 and weights decrement exactly.

test_vectors.vectors: Arrival order 8, 6, 4, 5, 7 with first sequence 4.
test_vectors.assertions: Repeated pops preserve missing sequences 5 and 7; output becomes 4 through 8 only when each gap arrives.

test_vectors.vectors: First sequence 7, buffered sequence 8, duplicate candidates 0, 6, 8 and previously emitted 7, 8.
test_vectors.assertions: DuplicateObjectKey precedes budget checks, including when the pending duplicate has become the exact next sequence. Original buffered completion survives.

test_vectors.vectors: Zero byte capacity, count capacity 2, zero-weight sequences 1, 2, 3.
test_vectors.assertions: Positive buffered weights fail, zero-weight entries still fill count capacity, and draining restores capacity.

test_vectors.vectors: Byte capacity 5; buffered weights 2, 3, 0; rejected candidate weight 2.
test_vectors.assertions: Exact capacity is accepted, over-budget insertion preserves state and completion, and the returned completion can be retried after draining.

test_vectors.vectors: Weights usize::MAX - 1, 2, 1, 0 with maximum count and byte limits.
test_vectors.assertions: Addition overflow returns BudgetExhausted without mutation, exact usize::MAX totals are supported, and direct delivery bypasses the full byte budget.

test_vectors.vectors: First and delivered sequence u64::MAX; subsequent attempts 0, u64::MAX - 1, u64::MAX.
test_vectors.assertions: Next becomes None without cancellation, further insertions are ConstraintViolation, and explicit cancellation subsequently takes precedence.

test_vectors.vectors: First sequence u64::MAX - 1 with u64::MAX buffered before its predecessor.
test_vectors.assertions: The maximum sequence is popped exactly once, duplicate pending-head insertion fails, and no wrap to zero occurs.

test_vectors.vectors: Sequences 20 through 23; a cancelled job at 21; SchemaVm TypeMismatch at byte 37, schema 11, field 19 at 22.
test_vectors.assertions: Successful, individually cancelled, and parser-failed results preserve sequence and diagnostics without cancelling the queue. Uses the canonical CancellationToken.

test_vectors.vectors: Error-valued completions subjected to old-sequence, pending-duplicate, budget, cancellation, and exhaustion rejection.
test_vectors.assertions: Original error metadata and declared weights survive rejected and direct delivery paths, including a failed u64::MAX completion.

test_vectors.vectors: Drop-tracked Rc-backed values across duplicate, budget, direct-delivery, and cancellation paths.
test_vectors.assertions: Owner identity is preserved, rejection does not drop the value, and every explicitly discarded owner drops exactly once.

test_vectors.vectors: Three buffered values, one directly delivered value, one popped value, repeated cancellation, and four subsequent rejected sequences.
test_vectors.assertions: Only still-buffered values are dropped by cancellation; delivered owners remain live, repeated cancellation is harmless, and an independent token is unchanged.

test_vectors.vectors: Empty queues starting at 0 and u64::MAX; a separate queue dropped with two buffered values.
test_vectors.assertions: Empty cancellation is permanent and idempotent; ordinary queue destruction releases buffered owners exactly once.

test_vectors.vectors: Admission capacities 3 jobs, 12 retained bytes, 6 scratch bytes; each admitted output reserves 1 job, 4 retained bytes, 2 scratch bytes.
test_vectors.assertions: Queue rejection, direct return, popping, and into_parts preserve leases; dropping owners or cancelling buffered results releases exact reservations. Full admission remains exhausted while delivered results are held.

test_vectors.vectors: Count limits 1 through 3, byte limits 0 through 3, every admissible held weight, candidate weights 0 through 4.
test_vectors.assertions: All 150 deterministic combinations match inclusive count and byte limits; rejected queues remain unchanged and direct head delivery always allows progress.

test_vectors.vectors: All 120 permutations of offsets 0 through 4 at first sequences 0, 41, u64::MAX - 4, for 360 ordered delivery scenarios.
test_vectors.assertions: Every scenario emits five results in exact order, preserves one parser error and all weights, maintains queue invariants, and exhausts correctly at the sequence boundary.

test_vectors.vectors: Owned byte vector [0, 1, 127, 128, 255] buffered behind an error completion.
test_vectors.assertions: Pointer identity and byte contents survive buffering and delivery. Compile-time Send assertions cover queues, completions, and insertion errors containing Admitted<Payload>.

test_vectors.vectors: An admitted buffered result whose destructor deliberately panics, under panic=unwind.
test_vectors.assertions: Caught unwinding leaves the queue empty and cancelled, releases its admission lease, and permits harmless repeated cancellation.

status.validation: Source reviewed against frozen contract and root layouts. Compilation, formatting, builds, checks, and test execution were not run, as instructed.
status.allocation_behavior: BTreeMap has no stable fallible reservation or insertion; buffered insertion uses standard allocation-failure behavior. Declared weights are accounting, not allocation measurements.
status.scope: Only crates/jmax-nagoya/src/ordered.rs and reports/wave4/W4-29.json were written. No new dependencies or unsafe code were added.
